$comment: THE SURFACE-READINESS LIST (epic cinatra#3155). A wave of the lifecycle-drawing driver program may drive only what the DEFAULT BRANCH ships. Every aspect a wave grounded and could NOT drive is recorded here, with the reason and, where there is one, the pull request that lands it — never stubbed, never approximated through a different control. A wave MAY still drive a reading that is not one of those aspects at all — a shared identity the default branch already draws — and records it in that wave's `driven` block; a driver recorded there binds no field, no action and no state, so it never contradicts an entry below it. scripts/design/__tests__/surface-readiness.test.mjs re-proves every entry against the tree on every run, so an entry that has become false (the control shipped) is a RED rather than a stale note: the list retires itself.

waves.summary: The eight in-conversation review cards for an individual artifact kind. Grounded one aspect at a time against the default branch: no first-party control carries either floor action the drawing declares, no per-kind card is drawn anywhere, and the per-kind readings that do exist are drawn inside the review card's credentialed island frame. What the wave CAN drive, it drives: seven of the eight surfaces take the header-only driver family recorded in `driven` below, which machine-checks the immutable target header the review screen's drawing declares at §IV — the one reading every kind shares, and the one the default branch already ships. That driver binds no field, no action and no state, so every entry below stands exactly as it was: the fields, actions and states recorded here are still unshipped, still re-proved against the tree on every run, and still wait for the landings each entry names. Nothing is stubbed and nothing is approximated through the header. The eighth surface, drupal-pointer-never-a-review-target, takes no driver and no allowlist exemption.

driven.reading: The immutable target header of the review screen's drawing, §IV: the artifact's display title, the type tag and the type id on the mono meta line beneath it, the pinned representation revision with its pinned marker, every row fact the host authorized, and the header's inertness — no edit control, no link, no revision picker inside it.
driven.why: The header is the one reading these seven kinds share and the only one of their readings the default branch already draws, so it is driven over the SHIPPED component through a props-only mount whose rows seed a stored artifact row and never a finished reading — the product's own composer words the type tag, the elided revision and every row fact, so the driver exercises the chain composer to component rather than a component printing its own props back. It is not one of the aspects a readiness entry is about: the family declares no field, no action and no state binding at all, and the guard re-proves that from the driver source rather than taking it on trust. drupal-pointer-never-a-review-target is deliberately outside the family: its drawn identity line says it is not pinnable and is never a review target, while the shipped header draws the pinned marker unconditionally, so putting it through this family would assert of it a pinned header the drawing says it never has.

entries.why: The email body kind registers no artifact display on the default branch: its package declares field renderers for the mid-run form and no display block at all, so nothing draws this binding for a reviewer to read.

The control for this pair NOW SHIPS: the review floor landed on pull request 3100 and declares it in the two files named above, so the earlier claim that no first-party module carries it has stopped being true and is not restated here. What still keeps the surface undriven is the reason its other two entries give and this one may not repeat: the card for this artifact kind is not drawn at all, so there is nothing for the floor to sit under. The wave that draws the card drives the pair over the shipped floor rather than approximating it through another control; until then this entry pins WHERE the control lives, and goes red if it moves, spreads or disappears.

No first-party module draws a card for this artifact kind at all: the surface's conformance anchor appears in the manifest and nowhere else in the tree. Until something draws the surface, its readings have nothing to be states of.

Every per-kind reading of a review target is drawn by a SERVER component inside the review card's own credentialed island frame, which the card addresses through a single-use, authorised URL. A props-only harness mount cannot reach it, and this harness substitutes no transport of any kind.

The pointer kind registers no artifact display on the default branch. The surface's own claim — that a pointer is never what a decision binds — IS shipped and is pinned elsewhere: the pointer type declares itself unpinnable with external mutability, the platform refuses any other disposition for an external pointer, and a decision binds the immutable snapshot record instead. What the drawing adds and the product does not have is a card that SAYS so where a reader can see it.
